writing.exampleCaption: The reservation is cheap; the first touch is what costs.
writing.explanation: The MMU maps pages of your address space onto physical frames, so allocating memory usually just reserves address range. Touching a page for the first time causes a page fault the kernel resolves by finding a frame — which is why a large allocation can be instant and the first write to it slow. It also explains mmap, copy-on-write after fork, and why RSS is smaller than virtual size.
writing.feedback: Read-only file mappings share frames through the page cache.
